name: Platysmaplasty (neck band surgery)
lead: Platysmaplasty is a surgical procedure that modifies the platysma, the thin sheet of muscle across the front of the neck, to reduce visible vertical neck bands and improve the neck contour. It is usually performed as part of a neck lift or facelift, sometimes together with removal of submental fat [1][4][6].

Published literature consists mainly of surgeons' technique descriptions and case series. Techniques include midline plication, muscle resection or transection, and the corset platysmaplasty, which was described in 1990 to address persistent bands and contour irregularities seen after earlier methods [1]. Hematoma is described as the most common complication of related facelift surgery [2]. In looksmaxxing communities it is grouped with hardmaxxing procedures aimed at a sharper jawline and neck.

paras: Surgeons modify the platysma by tightening it at the midline, resecting or cutting it, or suturing it in a corset-like pattern [1]. Limited-incision approaches combining submental lipectomy with platysmaplasty have also been published [6]. Anatomical work has analysed platysma suspension during neck lift in a series of 30 cases [9]. A surgeon's 2014 update describes a neck lift strategy aiming to control the size, shape and position of each neck feature, drawing on 522 consecutive procedures [4].

A review of 1078 consecutive facelifts examined factors associated with hematoma, described as the most common complication of rhytidectomy and a cause of prolonged swelling or skin necrosis [2]. A preliminary report described local infiltration of tranexamic acid to reduce intraoperative bleeding during facelifts [3]. Persistent or recurrent bands, visible submandibular gland bulges and contour irregularities were the shortcomings that prompted the corset technique [1].

Thread-lift sutures and barbed sutures have been reviewed as less invasive options in aesthetic surgery [5][8]. A paired report of identical twins undergoing facelifts with different techniques gave 10-year follow-up comparison [10].

Evidence is largely retrospective case series and technique papers rather than randomized trials. Reported examples include a 1078-facelift hematoma review [2], 522 neck lifts reviewed by one surgeon [4], a 30-case anatomical analysis [9], and a 10-year twin comparison [10]. A systematic review of thread-lift sutures concerns a related, less invasive approach [5].

timeline.event: Corset platysmaplasty described in Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery [1].
Limited-incision submental lipectomy with platysmaplasty reported [6].
A surgeon publishes an update on his neck-lift approach based on 522 cases [4].

card.summary: Surgery that tightens the neck's platysma muscle to remove bands and sharpen the neck line; supported by surgical case series, not trials.
card.aka: Neck lift muscle tightening, corset platysmaplasty
card.note: Real surgery with hematoma and other operative risks; evidence is mostly surgeon case series.

quick.overview:
Platysmaplasty tightens or reshapes the platysma muscle in the neck to reduce vertical bands and improve contour. It is usually done within a neck lift or facelift.

The published evidence is mainly surgeons' technique papers and case series; no randomized trials were found.
quick.mechanism: Surgeons plicate, cut or suture the platysma, for example in a corset pattern, so the muscle sits flatter and tighter beneath the skin.
quick.risks: Hematoma is the most common complication of related facelift surgery; persistent bands and contour irregularities have been reported with some techniques. It is performed by surgeons under anesthesia.
